_readme: Rate inputs for the fixed-or-variable simulator. Every number here is sourced line by line in docs/research/2026-09-10-fixed-or-variable/notes/historical-rates.md — do not edit this file without updating that note. Offers are best broadly available INSURED (high-ratio) rates, one consistent basis across all dates; uninsured ran roughly 25-30 bp higher in 2021 and 2023, which shifts both columns and not the verdict.
_overnight_note: Bank of Canada target for the overnight rate, by EFFECTIVE date (announcement + 1 business day). Cross-checked against BoC Valet V39079, the BoC policy-rate page and nesto. Big-bank prime = this + 2.20 at every point in the window; TD's mortgage prime is a further +0.15.
_offers_note: Best broadly available insured (high-ratio) rates at each signing month, from archived Ratehub captures; varDisc is the discount off prime, so the contract rate is prime - varDisc. Per-cell provenance and flags in notes/historical-rates.md sections 3A-3E. Two months carry a known artifact: the simulator charges each month the prime in force on its FIRST day, but the 2022-06 and 2024-06 captures postdate a prime change that month, so the first month's variable rate runs 50bp / 25bp high respectively. Every later month is unaffected.

2022-01.src: Ratehub main 2022-01-13; 3y from Big-5 'best market rate' row, insured basis inferred

2022-06.src: Ratehub 2022-06-12; 3y basis inferred. NB capture-date prime was 3.70 (Jun 2 change); month-start convention uses 3.20

2024-01.src: Ratehub 2024-01-13; 5y is the national best (table-topper was Quebec-only); 3y is Ratehub's anonymised 'Big 6 Bank' row

2024-06.src: Ratehub 2024-06-14; 5y national best; 3y 'Big 6 Bank'. NB capture-date prime was 6.95 (Jun 6 cut); month-start convention uses 7.20

_conversions_note: Mid-term lock-ins: what an existing variable borrower was actually offered to convert to a fixed rate. Lenders price conversion off POSTED rates, well above the market best (Ratehub's worked scenario: 6.64% convert vs 5.79% refinance). Only one 2022 figure is documented rather than bracketed, so only one is listed.

conversions.src: Global News, 17 Sept 2022 - brokers reporting clients locking in around 4.7% (range to 5.39%, one at 4.69%), against posted 6.14% and market-best 4.29-4.44%
